title: Achyutashtakam
intro: Achyutashtakam is a devotional hymn dedicated to Lord Vishnu (Achyuta), praising His divine attributes and names.
description:
I worship Achyuta, Kesheva, Rama, Narayana, Krishna, Damodara, Vasudeva, Hari, Sridhara, Madhava,
the beloved of the Gopis, the lord of Janaki, and Ramachandra.

I meditate upon Achyuta, Kesheva, the beloved of Satyabhama, Madhava, Sridhara, the one worshipped by Radha,
the dwelling place of Indira, beautiful to the heart, the son of Devaki, and the son of Nanda.

Salutations to Vishnu, the victorious, the bearer of the conch and the discus, the lover of Rukmini, the husband of Janaki,
the inner soul worshipped by the Gopis, the destroyer of Kamsa, and the wielder of the flute.

Oh Krishna, Govinda, Rama, Narayana, Shripate, Vasudeva, Ajita, Shrinidhe, Achyutananta, Madhava, Adhokshaja,
the lord of Dwaraka, and the protector of Draupadi, I bow to You.

Troubled by demons, adorned with Sita, the purifier of the Dandaka forest, accompanied by Lakshmana, served by the army of monkeys,
and worshipped by Sage Agastya—oh Raghava, please protect me.

The destroyer of fierce enemies like Dhenuka and Arishtasura, the slayer of Kesi, the captivator of Kamsa’s heart, the player of the flute,
the tormentor of Putana, who played on the banks of the Yamuna—may the child Gopala protect me always.

I worship the lotus-eyed Lord whose garments shine like lightning, whose divine form glows like a rain-bearing cloud,
whose chest is adorned with a garland of forest flowers, and whose two feet are reddish.

I worship the dark-complexioned Lord whose radiant face is framed by curved locks of hair, who wears a gem-studded crown, glittering earrings on His cheeks,
shining armlets and bracelets, and a sweet-sounding girdle of bells around His waist.

I worship Achyuta, Kesheva, Ramanarayana, Krishna Damodara, Vasudeva, Hari, Sridhara, Madhava,
the beloved of the Gopis, the lord of Janaki, and Ramachandra.

Whoever reads this sacred Ashtakam of Achyuta daily with devotion, desire, and pure intent,
Lord Hari quickly becomes favorable and yields to that devotee.

faq.a1: Achyutashtakam was composed by the great philosopher and saint Adi Shankaracharya.
faq.a2: "Achyuta" is a sacred name of Lord Vishnu meaning "the infallible one"—one who never slips from His essential nature or supreme status.
faq.q3: What are the benefits of reciting Achyutashtakam?
faq.a3: Regular recitation brings the grace and protection of Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna, dispels fears and hardships, and fills the devotee's heart with peace and devotion.
faq.q4: When is the best time to recite Achyutashtakam?
faq.a4: It is ideal to recite it during morning prayers or on holy days like Ekadashi, though it can be chanted anytime with absolute devotion.
